svg.title: One opaque query versus three named, chainable models doing the identical work
svg.desc: Before: a single monolithic SQL query reads directly from raw.trips and computes a daily trip count and revenue total in one opaque step, with no named boundary between cleaning the data, aggregating it, and rolling it up -- any other question needing the same cleanup has to copy the whole query. After: the identical work split into three models chained by ref(). stg_trips cleans and relabels columns from the source. int_hourly_pattern aggregates by hour and zone, reusable on its own for time-of-day questions. daily_summary rolls int_hourly_pattern up to a daily total. Each model does one named job and can be read, tested, or reused independently, and a fourth model, zone_revenue, can branch off stg_trips too -- something the one-query version had no way to express.
svg.text: One Opaque Query vs. Three Named Models
The identical work, computing the identical daily total -- structured two different ways
Before: One Query
select
date_trunc('day', pickup_time) as pickup_day,
count(*) as trip_count,
round(sum(total_amount), 2) as daily_revenue
from raw.trips
group by 1;
-- cleanup, aggregation, and rollup, all in one place
No named boundary between cleaning columns,
aggregating by hour, and rolling up to a day.
A second question needing the same cleanup
has to copy this whole query to get it.
split apart
After: Three Named Models
stg_trips -- cleans & relabels
int_hourly_pattern -- aggregates by hour
daily_summary -- rolls up to a day
Each model has one named job, readable,
testable, and reusable on its own --
zone_revenue branches off stg_trips too,
something one query had no way to express.
Both versions compute the identical answer: 81,013 trips, $2,442,843.25 -- structure changed, not the result.
